Decompose a treatment effect into mediated and calibrated contrasts

Source: R/calibrated-contrasts.R
calibrated_contrasts.Rd

Given estimates of the risk of an outcome under treatment, under placebo, and under a calibrated intervention (as returned by tmle_alpha() and calibrate_alpha()), computes the total treatment effect and its decomposition into a mediated contrast (treatment versus calibrated) and a calibrated contrast (calibrated versus placebo), with Wald confidence intervals based on the influence curves.

Usage

calibrated_contrasts(treatment_fit, placebo_fit, calibrated_fit, level = 0.95)

Arguments

treatment_fit, placebo_fit

Fits for the treatment and placebo arms, as returned by tmle_alpha() with different baseline treatments a.

calibrated_fit

Fit for the calibrated intervention, as returned by calibrate_alpha() with the a of treatment_fit. It may contain estimates for several targets; the one of treatment_fit is used.

level

Number between 0 and 1. Confidence level of the intervals.

Value

An object of class calibrated_contrasts, a list with elements:

  • estimate: a data.table with one row per contrast (total, mediated and calibrated) and columns target, contrast, estimate, se, lower and upper.

  • target and level: the target and the confidence level.

  • checks: a list with decomposition_error and eic_decomposition_error, how far the estimates and influence curves are from satisfying total = mediated + calibrated, which should be zero up to numerical error.

Examples

# illness_death with a randomised treatment A0 added, for illustration.
set.seed(1)
treated <- illness_death
treated$A0 <- rbinom(max(treated$id), 1, 0.5)[treated$id]

fit <- fit_initial(
  treated,
  fit_types = list(
    z = list(
      delta = 2,
      model = ~ L0 + A0,
      at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0
    ),
    death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + A0 + z),
    censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~L0)
  ),
  tau = 1,
  treatment_model = A0 ~ L0
)

# How much of the effect of treatment on death is mediated by its effect
# on the risk of z?
calibrated_contrasts(
  treatment_fit = tmle_alpha(fit, target = "death", a = 1),
  placebo_fit = tmle_alpha(fit, target = "death", a = 0),
  calibrated_fit = calibrate_alpha(
    fit,
    target = "death",
    z_name = "z",
    value = 1,
    scale = "ratio",
    a = 1,
    reference_a = 0
  )
)
#> Decomposition of the effect of a on death into mediated and calibrated contrasts
#> 
#>    target   contrast   estimate         se       lower      upper
#>    <char>     <char>      <num>      <num>       <num>      <num>
#> 1:  death      total -0.1405813 0.07724416 -0.29197704 0.01081449
#> 2:  death   mediated -0.0234265 0.01632300 -0.05541899 0.00856599
#> 3:  death calibrated -0.1171548 0.08141345 -0.27672220 0.04241266
